purpose: Demonstrate different constellation architecture classes without claiming end-to-end independence.
researchConclusion: Different constellation architecture classes are represented. End-to-end infrastructure independence remains UNKNOWN.

scope.label: Catalogue + public architecture-class comparison (no site binding)
scope.geographicNote: Not bound to a specific Nordic/Arctic site pin

evidence.title: GRYPS Advisor / indexed provider catalogue
evidence.claim: Starlink and OneWeb are distinct catalogue ids; both LEO broadband; operators SpaceX and Eutelsat OneWeb in the display index.
evidence.limitations: No gateway, backhaul, or site fields.

evidence.title: Starlink Technology — optical laser mesh (architecture class)
evidence.claim: Current Starlink satellites are described as using optical inter-satellite links (architecture class).
evidence.limitations: Not a site-specific gateway or PoP map; not proof of dual-path independence with OneWeb.

evidence.title: OneWeb bent-pipe / gateway-dependent architecture class (secondary literature)
evidence.claim: OneWeb user literature / technical comparisons describe bent-pipe designs without ISL requiring gateway visibility (architecture class).
evidence.limitations: Architecture class only; does not identify gateways for a GRYPS site.

claimsNotToMake: End-to-end path independence between Starlink and OneWeb
Independence of ground infrastructure, backhaul, operations, or site power
That catalogue-based orbit mix is true for this pair (it is false in v0.4)
That ISL vs bent-pipe proves site dual-path continuity
Any resilience score, grade, weight, or failure probability
limitations: No GroundFacility or TerrestrialBackhaul entities are instantiated — inventing them would fabricate evidence.
Fixture is research-only and must not be treated as an operational assessment.
